newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan plans luxury cruise to disputed islands.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan plans luxury cruise to disputed islands.

text.p: A Taiwan travel agency hopes to cash in on a territorial dispute embroiling Taipei, Tokyo and Beijing by offering a luxury cruise to a group of disputed East China Sea islands.

The United Evening News said on Wednesday a firm in southern Kaohsiung would rent a 7,000-tonne cruise ship to sail to the deserted islands claimed by China and Taiwan as the Diaoyus and by Japan as the Senkakus.
Some 2,000 voyagers will have the chance to indulge in two days of fine dining, movies and even a shipboard karaoke lounge for just T$1,500-2,000 (US$56-74) per person, the newspaper said.
The initial cruise aims to satisfy local curiosity about the islands and is timed to coincide with the October 10 national day of Taiwan's exiled Republic of China.
Japanese patrol boats have been repelling vessels trying to land Taiwan and Hong Kong protesters on the islands and it was not known how close the cruise ship would try to sail.

Anti-Japan activists plan to approach the Diaoyus again on Sunday, the latest in a wave of protests sweeping Hong Kong, Taiwan, Macau and China since July, when a Japanese right-wing group built a lighthouse and raised Japan's flag on the islands to assert Tokyo's sovereignty.

The row took on new urgency with the September 26 death of Hong Kong activist David Chan, who drowned in a protest dive into waters near the islands after his boat was turned away by Japanese patrols.
Japan took the islands as war booty after defeating imperial China in 1895 and says the dispute is not open for discussion.
China and Taiwan, separated by a civil war in 1949, say the islands have been Chinese territory for centuries and should have returned to Chinese rule after Japan's World War Two defeat.
In September, a Taiwan company launched a virtual-reality computer game in which Japan, Taiwan and China are drawn into war over the islands.
